You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Walmart Q2 Earnings Preview: Can the Safe Haven Amid Consumption Downgrade Support Wall Street’s High Valuation?

TEXT:
1.Investment Highlights Overview
Walmart will release its fiscal 2027 second-quarter results (covering May–July 2026) before the U.S. market opens on August 20, 2026. Wall Street consensus expects total revenue of approximately $188.8 billion (about +6.45% YoY ) and adjusted EPS of $0.75 (about +10.3% YoY ). Management’s own guidance is more conservative, calling for constant-currency net sales growth of 4%–5% and adjusted EPS of $0.72–$0.74. As a retail giant that serves more than half of the U.S. population’s consumption needs, this report is widely viewed as a key “barometer” of consumer spending willingness and macroeconomic conditions. The market is closely watching whether Walmart can continue to act as a safe haven in a consumption-downgrade environment and support its currently elevated valuation.
2. Four Key Focus Areas
Focus 1: Can U.S. Comparable Sales Maintain Resilience?
In an environment of consumption downgrade and elevated fuel prices, U.S. comparable sales (excluding fuel) is the core metric to watch. Consensus expects growth of around 3.7%, though some institutions have already lowered their forecasts to 3%–3.5%. The metric came in at +4.1% in Q1, with higher-income customers contributing notably. If Q2 can hold or beat expectations, it would confirm Walmart’s share advantages in essentials and value-oriented spending; a miss could raise concerns about slowing growth.
Focus 2: Contribution from High-Growth Businesses — E-commerce, Advertising, and Membership
E-commerce and advertising remain key drivers of profit-mix improvement. Global e-commerce has recently sustained double-digit growth, advertising has grown even faster, and membership (including Walmart+ and Sam’s Club) continues to expand. Whether these higher-margin businesses can continue to offset pressure on traditional retail profitability will directly affect the operating margin’s path toward 5%+ and is an important pillar supporting valuation.
Focus 3: Room for Guidance Raises and Full-Year Expectation Gap
Management’s full-year adjusted EPS guidance stands at $2.75–$2.85, while Wall Street consensus is around $2.89, creating a modest expectation gap. A clear beat of the Q2 guidance midpoint accompanied by a constructive outlook could revive the classic “beat-and-raise” script; merely meeting the conservative guidance may put pressure on sen time nt given the elevated valuation.
Focus 4: Ability to Absorb Cost and Macro Pressures
Fuel costs, potential tariff impacts, and more cautious consumer behavior are the main variables. Management has previously indicated that Q2 operating profit growth may lag sales growth. Comments on second-half cost control, inventory health, and consumer segmentation (pressure on lower-income households versus resilience among higher-income customers) will shape how the market re-prices full-year certainty.
3. Risks and Opportunities Coexist
Upside Catalysts:
U.S. comparable sales and total revenue significantly above consensus, confirming share gains amid consumption downgrade.
Continued strong growth in e-commerce, advertising, and membership that drives operating-margin improvement and leads to a full-year guidance raise.
Management delivers a constructive second-half outlook that reinforces the “safe-haven” narrative and supports valuation recovery.
Downside Risks:
Comparable sales or overall growth merely meets or falls short of company guidance, raising questions about growth sustainability.
Operating profit growth lags sales meaningfully, with cost pressures or margins missing expectations.
Weaker macro consumer data or profit-taking under high valuation amplifies near-term volatility.
4. Trading Strategy Suggestions
Bullish Case: If core sales and profit data beat consensus and management raises full-year guidance while highlighting e-commerce/advertising contributions, it could strengthen confidence in Walmart as a defensive consumer leader and support valuation recovery.
Bearish Risk: If results are merely in-line or guidance is cautious, and given recent pressure on the stock, profit-taking could occur—especially amid broader retail-sector volatility.
Key Data to Watch:
Total revenue and year-over-year growth
U.S. comparable sales growth (excluding fuel)
Adjusted EPS and operating profit performance
Whether full-year guidance is raised, plus e-commerce/advertising growth rates
